fields.mechanism: Excessive no-load current caused by an air gap length deviation or rotor eccentricity increases core losses and magnetizing reactive power, generating heat in the stator windings despite balanced phase resistance and stable supply voltage.
fields.intervention: Measure the physical air gap clearance at multiple circumferential points using a feeler gauge with the rotor blocked, then re-shim or re-machine the bearing housings to restore uniform concentricity and nominal air gap length.
fields.expected_effect: Magnetizing current decreases to the nameplate no-load value, core losses normalize, and winding temperature remains below the thermal overload trip threshold during extended no-load operation.
fields.falsification_test: Clamp a true-RMS ammeter on each supply phase during no-load running; if the measured no-load current is less than 40 percent of the full-load rated current and the motor does not trip after 30 minutes, the mechanism is disproven.
